brief: Goldman derivatives trader Brian Garrett published a chart he calls possibly his "chart of the year": almost half of S&P 500 stocks now have a negative beta to the index itself, an all-time high by a significant margin. Garrett attributes this to index concentration driven by AI capex and tech dominance, though he says that is not the only explanation. He warns the dynamic can raise the risk of factor-level momentum unwinds like July's, while the index itself is now providing more diversification against a risk-off unwind than it has historically; that diversification effect also explains the spread between index and single-stock convexity (.VIXVIXEQ). Citing Goldman strategist Christian Mueller-Glissman's related note, Garrett says that if the phenomenon reverses, long S&P index wings and long correlation trades should work. To hedge for that reversal now, the desk likes RSP-outperformance-versus-SPX options (~65% implied correlation) and puts on the GS momentum index (GSP1MOMO), which imploded during July's factor unwind.
